runs.scenario_id: getInstance after close hands out a usable broadcaster whose broadcast never throws

test.oracle_basis_ref: broadcast.ts FallbackChannel jsdoc: graceful degradation without crashes; getInstance() is the only way to obtain a broadcaster so it must return a working instance

inputs.sequence: getInstance(), close(), getInstance() again, then broadcast a model-patched message

runs.expected: Broadcasting through an instance obtained after close() does not throw, because the singleton either reinitializes its channel or degrades to a no-op.

test.oracle_basis_ref: cache-manager.ts updateSnapshot(): cached snapshot object is reused when nothing changed so external-store consumers can compare by reference

inputs.sequence: read snapshot twice while loading, updateWithData({v:1}), read snapshot twice again

runs.expected: Repeated reads return the same snapshot object until a mutation happens, and updateWithData produces exactly one new snapshot carrying the data with success status.

runs.scenario_id: staleness boundaries: fresh data not stale, zero ttl always stale, untouched manager stale with infinite age

test.oracle_basis_ref: cache-manager.ts ModelHistory semantics: isStale means age reached the ttl; DEFAULT_HISTORY declares age Infinity and isStale true before any data arrives

inputs.managers: ttl 60000 updated now, ttl 0 (degenerate boundary) updated now, ttl 60000 never updated

runs.expected: Data updated just now is not stale under a 60s ttl, a zero ttl marks data stale immediately, and an untouched manager reports stale history with infinite age and null data.
